chapter_theme: Having tested someone, how to use them: match person, means, task and time, hand the work over fully, and don't resent the familiarity it brings, yet look at their conduct every day. Trust and scrutiny are both required, and the chapter doesn't entirely settle how.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar's divisions: who is fit for employment (511-513), who is to be excluded (514), the nature of work (515), how to employ them (516-519), and what to do after they are employed (520).

511.reading: One whose nature, having looked at good and bad, has settled on the good is to be employed.
511.nuance: Note the sequence: this person also looks at the bad. The verse doesn't ask for innocence. Parimelazhagar finds in the past tense புரிந்த a probationary stage: a trial task given first, then a more important one.

512.reading: Let him do the work who enlarges the sources, increases the yield and looks into what befalls them.
512.nuance: A purely administrative definition of a good servant, with no moral term. உற்றவை includes, for Parimelazhagar, what comes from the king himself, whose interference counts among the hazards.

513.reading: Trust lies in one who firmly has these four: love, understanding, clarity and freedom from desire.
513.nuance: Love comes first, even after the warnings of 507. Parimelazhagar directs it to the king and places the absence of desire at the moment when money comes into his hands, which is a very specific temptation.

514.reading: Even when trusted after every kind of test, many people turn different through the nature of the work.
514.nuance: The cause of change is the job itself, வினைவகையான். Office alters the person. Parimelazhagar's example is Kattiyankaran, the treacherous minister of Jivaka Chintamani, and he says it is rare for people to resist the pleasures of royal power.

515.reading: Work itself isn't such as to be given to anyone except one who knows and endures and can do it, just because he is favoured.
515.nuance: The grammar makes வினை the subject. Work has its own nature and doesn't admit of favourites. Parimelazhagar takes சிறந்தான் as someone dear to the king, and Kalaignar as someone merely thought excellent.

516.reading: Examine the doer, examine the deed, and act understanding how they fit with the time.
516.nuance: The doer comes before the deed, which is not the expected order. Parimelazhagar's last step is a judgment on the conjunction: at this time, one of this quality doing a deed of this nature will succeed.

517.reading: Having reasoned 'this one will finish this by this means', leave that to him.
517.nuance: The verse is all pointing, with இதனை, இதனால், இவன், then அதனை, அவன். The distal pronouns of the second line themselves enact the handing over: the thing moves away from the king. விடல் is a real letting go.

518.reading: After seeing a person is fit for the work, make him fully entitled to it.
518.nuance: Recognition isn't enough: authority has to be conferred. Parimelazhagar makes it elevation so that he can carry the work out himself, and warns that without it the work fails. Kalaignar reads this as simply examining then appointing, which leaves it close to 517.

519.reading: Fortune leaves one who takes differently the closeness of a person devoted to the work.
519.nuance: A rare observation about what success at work produces: familiarity. Parimelazhagar's setting is sharp: rivals tell the king this man acts as if he were family, and the king takes it as disrespect. If he punishes it, no one will commit themselves again.

520.reading: Let the ruler look into it daily: if the one doing the work doesn't bend, the world won't bend.
520.nuance: Parimelazhagar sees the difficulty with trust and adds that the inspection should be done privately, without harming the person's entitlement.

positions.position: The ruler inspects the officer's conduct. The officer is the one point through which the whole world can be checked.
positions.quote: வினை செய்வான் கோடாது ஒழிய உலகம் கோடாது;

positions.position: The state checks on workers' condition. If those who labour don't wither, the world's prosperity doesn't wither.

links.note: 510 says doubting one you have trusted brings endless trouble. 520 says inspect him every day. Parimelazhagar sees this and calls for private inspection, but the problem of watching without doubting remains.

501 builds an elaborate test and, in Parimelazhagar's words, passing shows the person won't change. 514 says that many change anyway, through the work itself. The most careful selection can't test for what office will do.

The king creates, gathers, guards and apportions in 385; the officer enlarges, increases and watches in 512. Parimelazhagar connects them. The servant's job is a copy of the master's, without the giving.
507 condemns trusting on fondness alone. 513 puts love first among four qualities, so the fault in 507 lies in the 'alone', not in the love.

source_issues: 513: Parimelazhagar's gloss prints தோற்றம் for the verse's தேற்றம், and its meaning, not wavering, fits தேற்றம். This appears to be a transcription slip.
515: The Manakkudavar entry is marked [#] and is nearly identical to Parimelazhagar's, so I did not treat it as independent.
517: The Parimelazhagar entry repeats its bracketed note twice.
